title: Review as a plan — headless code review, review-plan, run --append

ground.note: The first draft, Abandoned 2026-09-25. I reused its structure. The brief, revised 2026-09-25. It covers dismissal as a decision, two modes, the landed review doctrine, reversibility as a cost, and the five open questions to arbitrate.

The agent answers `version: 1`, then a verdict (conformant | conformant-with-deviations | divergent) and perPhase findings { dimension, severity info | deviation | concern, message }, decoded strictly with excess properties rejected. phax persists `compliance-review.json` with `$schema` `compliance-review` and no `version`.

RunState: created, running, failed, review_open, completed, stopped, archived, interrupted, rate_limited. Existing transitions include running → review_open and review_open | completed → archived. Nothing returns a run to running.

The short PR body (`buildShortPrBody`) holds a summary, `## Phases`, `## Needs your review` (compliance attention points, unexplained deviations), `## Review notes` and `## Full detail`, capped at 60,000 bytes (`PR_BODY_MAX_BYTES`). It cuts unexplained deviations, then attention points, then review notes. The summary, the phase lines and Full detail are never cut.
Completed. §5.1 says the body holds only its five sections; this spec amends it with a `### Review passes` subsection under `## Needs your review` for a run with a review pass.

Reuse-or-create: an existing PR for the branch is reused, and its body is not rebuilt. The body is built only when a PR is created, from `loadReviewHandoffInputs` (global reconciliation, phase handoffs, `source-spec-outcome.md`, review notes) plus `compliance-review.json`.
The run directory is <stateRoot>/runs/<key>, local and outside Git. It holds run-status.json, phax-plan.json, and one status.json per phase folder. The final phase is the highest-indexed one.

Exit families: 2 plan/config validation, 3 unsafe git state, 4 gate failed, 5 agent error or rejected document, 6 archive blocked by a dirty worktree, 7 lock, 8 rate/usage limit, 9 phase produced no changes, 10 registry corruption, 11 security or preflight refusal, 12 artifact or approval refusal, 1 otherwise.
`phax run [short-name] --plan <path>`, `review-code <short-name> [--new-session] [--model] [--effort]`, `publish-pr` (create or reuse), and `ls` filters. The registry is under ~/.phax/runs/.

Lists headless-review under the steme experiment specs, after plan-estimate. It names the rework this revision does: the short PR body replaced the body this spec built on, and the decision class was dropped. The oracle-separation lint is what makes review-as-plan safe.

The end of a run: run completion on the run branch (`completeRunArtifacts`), then `review_open`, then the compliance review when enabled (a failure is non-fatal: the run stays `review_open`), then `publish.auto` when set.

Run completion (spec 27). The plan goes Approved → Completed, and the source spec goes too when the plan says `completes-spec: true` and the chain gate allows. The chain gate (`findDependentPlans` in `src/app/artifactStatus.ts`) keeps the spec while another plan of it is still Approved. Committed on the run branch.
Inside a phase worktree, the guard refuses `run`, `artifact approve`, `artifact abandon`, `artifact new plan` and every other command that moves a run or an artifact.
`lineageFindings` errors when a plan's slug differs from its source spec's. `sequenceGapFindings` errors on every id missing from phase-01 up to the highest phase.
Plan frontmatter has two variants: spec-less (`source-spec: null`), and spec-bound with a required `completes-spec`. Unknown keys are rejected.

The plan document (`kind: plan`, `$schema` `plan-document`). Its fields: lineage (`sourceSpec`, `completesSpec`), `run`, a preamble with open and arbitrated questions, and phases with boundary contracts, implementation order, verification and expected handoff. Its projection is the extracted-plan schema.
The approver union: operator, machine (grant `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`) and unattributed (records written before approvers were named).
Every persisted format carries a `$schema` URL `<base>/<format-id>/<X.Y.Z>.json`. `code-review` is expected to join with this spec's plan.

The brief of this revision, 2026-10-23. A review finding says from which angle it was found and why the run's tests did not catch it, so the review feeds the test strategy back. It settles the three keys, the shared vocabulary, the headless session following `phax-review`, and no migration, and leaves four questions to §9.

The review skill (commit 1259ec48). The reviewer uses the change before reading its code and works outside-in. Every finding gives where, what is wrong for whom, a severity, a `lens` (the step it was found in: surface, acceptance, boundary, core, edge, tests, architecture, docs), an `escape` (why the tests missed it: wrong-oracle, same-author, weakened, fake-drift, unexplored-input, omission, untestable), the criterion it touches and a suggestion. A `wrong-oracle`, `omission` or `unexplored-input` finding names the test line the plan should have carried.

`phax review-code` embeds `phax-review` in its prompt: the copy at `.claude/skills/phax-review/SKILL.md` in the run's final-phase worktree when it exists, else the bundled skill. `src/domain/review/codeReviewPrompt.ts` renders it under `## Review doctrine` with its source, `project` or `bundled`.

Completed, shipped in 0.28.0. A phase's test strategy is a list of test lines (guarantee, size, technique, oracle, loop, and a criterion id or none). A criterion id is the `id` of one of the source spec's acceptance criteria, read from the spec's JSON sidecar. `phax plans lint` reports an unknown id as an error and, when the spec has no sidecar, says so in one line and checks no criterion.

context:
`phax review-code <run>` opens an interactive, pre-prompted session in a `review_open` run's worktree. It resumes the session recorded in `code-review-session.json` unless `--new-session` is given, and the developer then takes over.

`phax review-compliance <run>` is its non-mutating, structured sibling. The review agent answers `{ version: 1, verdict: conformant | conformant-with-deviations | divergent, summary, perPhase[{ phaseId, verdict, findings[{ dimension, severity: info | deviation | concern, message }] }], attentionPoints, pointers }`, decoded strictly. phax persists it as `compliance-review.json`, `$schema` first and with no `version`, as it persists every format.

`phax.json` has `review.compliance.{enabled, model, effort}`. Under `review.code` it has only `{model, effort}`. The `publish` block is optional. When present, its `auto` key is required, and an absent block resolves to `auto: false`. With `auto` true, the run pushes its final branch and opens its PR once it is `review_open`.

A run lives in the local registry (`~/.phax/runs/`), outside Git. Its committed trace is the records branch `phax/records/v1`. `phax run [short-name] --plan <path>` gives each phase its own worktree on `phax/<slug>--phase-NN`. The last phase stays open in `review_open`, where manual fixes land as ordinary commits. The run states allow `running → review_open` and `review_open → archived`. Nothing returns a run to `running`.

The end of a run is, in order:
1. The final phase commits.
2. The run applies its run completion on the run branch (spec 27). Its plan goes Approved → Completed. Its source spec goes too, when the plan says `completes-spec: true` and the chain gate allows.
3. The run becomes `review_open`.
4. The compliance review runs, when enabled.
5. `publish.auto` publishes, when set.

Plan approval refuses a plan whose source spec is not Approved.

Runs stay autonomous (2026-10-10). A run never stops to wait for a person, and phase decision requests are parked unbuilt. Human input goes to the review notes.

Inside a phase worktree, the phase guard refuses `phax run`, `phax artifact approve`, `phax artifact abandon` and `phax artifact new plan`. Nothing an agent runs there moves a run or approves a plan.

Today's exit families:
- 2: plan or config validation
- 3: unsafe Git state
- 4: gate failure
- 5: agent error or rejected document
- 6: archive blocked by a dirty worktree
- 7: lock conflict
- 8: rate or usage limit
- 9: phase produced no changes
- 10: registry corruption
- 11: security or preflight refusal
- 12: artifact or approval refusal
- 1: anything else

`phax publish-pr` builds the short PR body of `src/domain/publish/prBody.ts` from the run's facts. It holds, in order:
- a summary: run, plan, gate profile, the source spec's outcome, phases passed, verified surfaces and compliance verdict;
- `## Phases`, one line per phase;
- `## Needs your review`: `### Compliance attention points` when the run was reviewed, then `### Unexplained deviations`;
- `## Review notes`, when there are notes;
- `## Full detail`, which points to `review-handoff.md`.

The handoff itself is not in the body. Over 60,000 bytes, the body cuts unexplained deviations, then attention points, then review notes; each cut run becomes one `- …and N more` line. The summary, the phase lines and Full detail are never cut. The body is built only when the PR is created: an existing PR for the branch is reused, not updated. Through `gh`, phax today only creates a PR ready for review. It never opens a draft, never marks a PR ready, and never edits a body. This spec adds those three GitHub operations, plus reading a PR's state (draft, ready, closed or merged): create a draft PR, mark a PR ready for review, and edit a PR's body.

Headless authoring set the pattern reused here. `phax artifact new plan <slug> --headless --brief <file> --spec <spec>` runs a session that returns only a schema-validated plan document. phax then:
- renders the Markdown deterministically;
- writes the document as the plan's JSON sidecar (`$schema` `plan-document`);
- seeds the extraction cache with the plan projection;
- commits with an `Authoring-Id` trailer;
- records the session.

`phax artifact approve`, `artifact status` and `artifact migrate-documents` decode that sidecar. They refuse a plan whose body diverges from its rendering.

The review doctrine landed by hand on 2026-09-25 as the skill `phax-decide-review`, now registered in the skill catalog. It holds principles `R1`–`R7` under the pairs `C1`–`C5` and the ground `E0`. Its headless sections still describe the earlier design: the agent decides within the menu, escalates the rest, and outputs `decisions[]` for the findings it escalates. Reversal is a cost: at equal value, the change that is cheaper to reverse is preferred, and a destructive change stops.

The `artifact-decide` spec (Completed, `docs/specs/archive/2610140742-artifact-decide.md`) shipped `phax artifact decide`, interactive only and Claude Code only. When the operator exits, phax resumes the session headless for the revised document and checks it. It then shows the body diff, and writes nothing unless the operator accepts it. It fixes three shapes this spec reuses:
- the decided verdict `{ kind: decided, chosen, abandoned[], why, advocate, principles[], reversibility: cheap | costly | irreversible, by: { kind: operator, name }, at, revised[] }`, stamped with the committing git identity and the time;
- principle ids, the backticked ids that open a doctrine's list items; a doctrine file that defines none, or redefines a skill id, is refused;
- the approver of `phax artifact approve --by operator | --by machine:<grant>`. The grant is a kebab-case slug, and the approver is recorded as `approvedBy` in the plan's approval record file, `docs/plans/approvals/<plan file stem>.json`. Without a terminal, approve refuses with exit 12 unless `--by` is given.

The first consumer is the steme roadmap-1.0 conductor. It is a loop with no developer at the terminal, and it allows at most two review passes.

The review itself has a doctrine since 2026-10-23, the skill `phax-review`, distinct from `phax-decide-review`, which governs what a review plan does with findings. `phax review-code` embeds it in its prompt: the project's copy in the run's final-phase worktree, else the bundled skill. It has the reviewer give every finding a `lens`, the step it was found in, an `escape`, why the run's tests did not catch it, and the acceptance criterion it touches. That vocabulary is prose only today.

Since 0.28.0 a plan's test strategy is data: test lines that may name an acceptance criterion of the source spec by its id, read from the spec's JSON sidecar, and a coverage of criteria by lines.
problem:
A loop has no developer, so it cannot run the only code review phax offers. Two shortcuts both fail:
- Printing the prompt for an outside agent takes the review out of phax. There is no run directory, no records and no resumable session, and the findings come back as prose.
- Resuming the review session with "fix everything" puts changes into the run without phases. Those changes get no gate of their own, no handoff and no reconciliation, and the session is free to edit the test that judges it.

Fixes that follow a review must go through the same machinery as the implementation, but a run cannot grow. Once a run is `review_open` it runs no further phase, and a second run means a second PR and a second records lineage.

A finding the reviewer got wrong has no home either. It is either fixed anyway, which is a wrong change, or left open forever. Nothing records that someone judged it wrong, or why.

Nothing bounds or reports the review–fix loop. The PR body says what needs a person's review. It does not say whether the run converged under review, or what was deliberately left unfixed.

The run also completes its plan and its spec at its final phase, before any review. A plan of fixes written after that has no Approved spec to belong to.

A finding has no angle and no cause either. The review skill asks for a `lens` and an `escape`, but a document of `{ severity, file, line, message, suggestion }` drops both. Nothing after the review can tell a finding that a missing test let through from one that no test could catch, so the review ends at a fix and never reaches the test strategy.

productGoal.statement:
Make the code review a phax artifact, and make its consequence a phax plan.

A headless review writes structured findings and stops. Each review finding says from which step it was found, why the run's tests missed it, and which acceptance criterion it touches. `phax review-plan` turns them into a review plan in the phax-plan shape, following a doctrine and a threshold that the caller owns. Each finding under consideration is either fixed by a phase or decided by the operator: dismissed or left open; one a headless plan does not fix waits, `awaiting`, for that decision. `phax run --append` then executes the plan as more phases of the same run, with the same records and the same PR.

A config setting runs this as a bounded loop at the end of a run, before the run completes its plan and spec and before its PR is ready for review. While a review plan or a finding waits for the operator, the run's PR is a GitHub draft. The PR's `## Needs your review` then opens on the trajectory: the review passes, and the findings that wait for the operator or that the operator dismissed. Every change is additive to the CLI and to `phax.json`, and the interactive review is unchanged.
productGoal.guidingRule: A review changes code only through phases of the same run. A machine may fix a finding but never settles one it does not fix. Every finding ends fixed, open, dismissed or awaiting, and none is dropped.

terminology.definition: One review round over a run, numbered from 1. A pass opens when a headless code review writes its `code-review.json`. It holds at most one current review plan. Its `code-review.json` and `pass.json` live under the run directory and in the run's records; its review plan lives under `docs/plans/` on the run branch (§9 Q4).

One entry of a pass's `code-review.json`. It has one of two variants, by `source`. A review finding (`review`) has `severity`, `file`, `line`, `lens`, `escape`, `criterion` and `suggestion`. A compliance finding (`compliance`) is a `deviation` finding of the latest compliance review, with `phase` and `dimension`, and has no `lens`, `escape` or `criterion`. Both carry `id`, `message`, `outcome` and `history`.

The skill a code-review session follows, `phax-review`: the copy at `.claude/skills/phax-review/SKILL.md` in the run's final-phase worktree, else the bundled skill. Distinct from the review doctrine, which a review-plan session follows.
The step of the review skill a review finding was found in: `surface`, `acceptance`, `boundary`, `core`, `edge`, `tests`, `architecture` or `docs`. Closed set, the skill's ids.
Why the run's tests did not catch a review finding: `wrong-oracle`, `same-author`, `weakened`, `fake-drift`, `unexplored-input`, `omission` or `untestable`. Closed set, the skill's ids.
The acceptance criterion a review finding touches: the `id` of one of the run's source spec's acceptance criteria, as a test line names it, or null when it touches none.
A run-unique id that phax assigns: `F<n>` for review findings and `C<n>` for compliance findings. Numbering continues from pass to pass.
`bug` > `deviation` > `concern` > `info`.
The lowest severity a pass considers for a fix: `bug`, `deviation` or `concern`. `info` is never considered.
In headless mode: the latest pass's findings at or above the threshold whose outcome is `open`. In interactive mode: those findings plus every `awaiting` finding of the run.

A finding's current state:
- `fixed`: a phase of an appended review plan names the finding and reached `committed`.
- `awaiting`: a headless review plan left it unfixed; it waits for an operator decision. It carries no proposal.
- `dismissed`: its last decision is an operator `dismiss`.
- `open`: anything else. This covers undecided findings, findings planned but not yet committed, operator `leave-open` decisions, below-threshold findings and `info` findings.

An operator's decision about a finding that no phase fixes, in the decided-verdict shape of `phax artifact decide` (`revised` is always empty for a finding). Its menu is `fix` | `dismiss` | `leave-open`: it chooses `dismiss` or `leave-open` and abandons the other two. A dismissal says why the finding is wrong. Decisions are made in interactive mode only, appended to the finding's `history`, and never rewritten.
The instructions a review-plan session follows: the `phax-decide-review` skill (a project-scoped skill of the same name replaces it), followed by the caller's doctrine file.

The plan a review-plan session emits for one pass. Its phases project to the extracted-plan schema and name the finding ids they fix. It also carries `decisions[]` (interactive only) and a handoff note. With at least one phase, phax writes it under `docs/plans/` on the run branch, as Markdown plus its sidecar: the plan document's `review-plan` variant. With no phase, phax writes no plan.

One of:
- `reviewed`: the headless review wrote the pass's findings, and no review plan has landed yet.
- `planned`: the review plan has phases.
- `no-fix`: no finding under consideration was planned (each was decided in interactive mode, or left awaiting in headless mode).
- `clean`: nothing was under consideration.
- `blocked-divergent`: the latest compliance verdict is `divergent`.
- `superseded`: a later pass opened while this pass's review plan was Draft, or Approved and not appended; that plan was abandoned.
- `failed`: a step of the loop failed in this pass (compliance review, headless review, review plan, loop approval, or the push after an append).
A phase executed by `phax run --append`. It is numbered after the run's existing phases, runs under the same run id, and has the origin `from review pass N`.
The union of every file declared by any plan the run executed (to create, to edit, or optional), plus the files named by the findings under consideration.

A file that judges the code a phase changes: a test, a fixture or a disposition matrix. `--append` does not identify oracle files; until the oracle-separation lint exists, the compliance review alone checks that a fix did not edit one (R4).
The cost of undoing a change or a decision: `cheap` | `costly` | `irreversible`. A review-plan phase is never `irreversible`, because destructive work stops.

An approval of a review plan whose `approvedBy` is `{ kind: machine, grant }`. It is recorded in the review plan's approval record file, `docs/plans/approvals/<plan file stem>.json`, on the run branch. The grant comes from `--by machine:<grant>`, or is `review-code-append` when the loop approves. An operator approval is `{ kind: operator, name }`.

The step of spec 27 that moves the run's plan, and its source spec when the plan completes it, to Completed on the run branch. With `review.code.enabled`, it runs when the run's PR becomes ready for review, after the last review pass, instead of at the final phase.

`--run <run>` on `phax artifact approve`, `artifact status` and `plans lint`. The command reads and writes the plan in that run's final-phase worktree and commits on the run branch, from the checkout. `phax run <run> --append` targets its run by the positional name.

A run's pull request opened as a GitHub draft because a review item is pending. It accepts appends, and after each one phax pushes the branch and rewrites the body, so the PR follows the run. `phax publish-pr` marks it ready for review once nothing is pending. A PR that is ready, closed or merged refuses appends. phax reads a PR's state live, through `gh`, whenever it needs it.

The end of the original `phax run --plan`, or of a `phax resume` of one of its original phases. Only a loop trigger starts review passes and `publish.auto`. An append, or a resume of an appended phase, starts neither.

requirements.title: Headless code review in the run's session
requirements.statement: WHERE `--headless` is given to `phax review-code <run>` THE system SHALL run the code review in the run's review session, in the run's final-phase worktree, without attaching a terminal. It SHALL resume the recorded session unless `--new-session` is given.

requirements.title: The review brief carries the review skill, compliance and earlier outcomes
requirements.statement: WHEN a headless review session starts THE system SHALL give it the review skill, the project's copy in the run's final-phase worktree when it exists and else the bundled `phax-review`, as `phax review-code` does. It SHALL also give the session the run's latest compliance verdict and findings, every earlier finding of the run with its outcome, and the source spec's acceptance criteria, id and name, when the spec has a JSON sidecar.

requirements.title: JSON-only code-review result
requirements.statement: WHEN a headless review session ends THE system SHALL accept as its result only a JSON code-review document valid against the code-review document schema. Every finding of the document SHALL carry `severity`, `file`, `line`, `message`, `lens`, `escape`, `criterion` and `suggestion`, all required: `lens` one of `surface`, `acceptance`, `boundary`, `core`, `edge`, `tests`, `architecture` or `docs`, `escape` one of `wrong-oracle`, `same-author`, `weakened`, `fake-drift`, `unexplored-input`, `omission` or `untestable`, and `criterion` an acceptance criterion id or null. The `lens` and `escape` values SHALL be exactly the ids that the bundled `phax-review` skill lists.

requirements.title: An invalid review opens no pass
requirements.statement: IF the headless review result is not JSON or fails validation THEN the system SHALL fail in the agent-error exit family, name the first violation path, and open no pass.

requirements.title: Run-unique finding ids
requirements.statement: The system SHALL give every finding a run-unique id, `F<n>` for a review finding and `C<n>` for a compliance finding, continuing the run's numbering from pass to pass.

requirements.title: Compliance deviations join the findings
requirements.statement: WHEN the system writes a pass's `code-review.json` THE system SHALL include each `deviation` finding of the run's latest compliance review as a compliance finding, with its `phase` and `dimension` and no `lens`, `escape` or `criterion`.

requirements.title: Write, record, stop
requirements.statement: WHEN the code-review document validates THE system SHALL open the next pass. It SHALL write the pass's `code-review.json`, with every finding at outcome `open` and each review finding's `lens`, `escape` and `criterion` as the session gave them, and its `pass.json`, with outcome `reviewed`, mode `none` and threshold null, under the run directory and into the run's records. It SHALL then stop, leaving the review session resumable and the run `review_open`.

requirements.title: A new pass supersedes a pending plan
requirements.statement: WHEN a pass opens while the previous pass's review plan is Draft, or Approved and not appended, THE system SHALL abandon that plan on the run branch, as a replaced plan is abandoned, and set the previous pass's outcome to `superseded`. That plan's findings keep their outcomes.

requirements.title: Review sessions write nothing outside .phax-context/
requirements.statement: The system SHALL run headless review and review-plan sessions under the read-only review security posture. Their sessions SHALL change no file of the worktree outside `.phax-context/`; phax alone writes the pass documents and the review plan.

requirements.title: Interactive review-code unchanged
requirements.statement: The system SHALL leave `phax review-code <run>` without `--headless` unchanged: it stays a conversation and writes no code-review document. A later `phax review-code <run> --headless` resumes the session it recorded, unless `--new-session` is given, and writes what it finds as a pass.

requirements.title: No pass on a completed run
requirements.statement: IF the run has applied its run completion THEN `phax review-code --headless` SHALL refuse before any session, naming the completion and `review.code.enabled`, the setting that keeps a run open to review passes.

requirements.title: Review-plan preconditions
requirements.statement: IF the run is not `review_open`, has no pass, has already appended its latest pass's review plan, or has applied its run completion, or the doctrine file is unreadable, defines no principle id or redefines a skill id, THEN `phax review-plan` SHALL refuse before any session, naming the condition.

requirements.title: review-plan is refused inside a phase worktree
requirements.statement: IF `phax review-plan` runs inside a phase worktree THEN the phase guard SHALL refuse it, as it refuses `review-code`: the command moves a run's artifacts, so its class is refused.

requirements.title: Review-plan session continuity
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax review-plan <run>` starts THE system SHALL resume the run's review session if its record exists, and otherwise start a new session from the latest pass's `code-review.json`.

requirements.title: Review doctrine skill
requirements.statement: The system SHALL load the `phax-decide-review` doctrine skill into every review-plan session. A project-scoped skill of the same name SHALL take the bundled skill's place.

requirements.title: The review doctrine's headless mode plans fixes only
requirements.statement: The bundled `phax-decide-review` skill SHALL instruct a headless session to plan fixes only and to leave unnamed every finding under consideration that it does not fix. Its headless sections SHALL carry no escalation, no proposal and no `decisions[]` output.

requirements.title: Caller doctrine appended
requirements.statement: WHERE a doctrine file is given by `--doctrine`, or else by `review.code.doctrine`, THE system SHALL append its content after the doctrine skill in the session prompt.

requirements.title: Threshold resolution
requirements.statement: The system SHALL consider for a fix only findings at or above the threshold. The threshold resolves from `--min-severity`, else `review.code.minSeverity`, else `concern`.

requirements.title: Info and below-threshold findings go to the handoff note
requirements.statement: The system SHALL gather the `info` findings and the below-threshold findings of every pass into one handoff-note list for the run, deduplicated by file and message and tagged with no pass or phase, because the review judges the run's whole change set; it SHALL never put them in a phase or a decision.

requirements.title: JSON-only review plan
requirements.statement: WHEN a review-plan session ends THE system SHALL accept as its result only a JSON review-plan document: `version: 1`, then the plan document's `review-plan` variant, whose phase projection is the extracted-plan schema.

requirements.title: Every finding under consideration is fixed or decided once
requirements.statement: IF, in an interactive review-plan document, a finding under consideration is named by no phase and no decision, or by more than one; or, in a headless document, a finding is named by more than one phase; or a phase or decision names a finding not under consideration, THEN the system SHALL reject the review-plan document, naming the finding.

requirements.title: Finding decisions follow the menu and cite the doctrine
requirements.statement: IF an operator decision does not choose `dismiss` or `leave-open`, does not abandon exactly the other two of `fix`, `dismiss` and `leave-open`, or cites a principle id that no loaded doctrine defines, THEN the system SHALL reject the review-plan document.

requirements.title: A headless plan decides nothing
requirements.statement: IF a headless review-plan document carries any decision THEN the system SHALL reject the document: a finding it does not fix is left awaiting the operator.

requirements.title: Destructive work stops
requirements.statement: IF a phase of the review plan is rated `irreversible` THEN the system SHALL reject the review-plan document.

requirements.title: An invalid review plan lands nothing
requirements.statement: IF the review-plan result is not JSON, fails validation, or is rejected by any check in this section THEN the system SHALL fail in the agent-error exit family and name the first violation path. It SHALL write nothing and change no finding's outcome.

requirements.title: Phases continue the run's numbering
requirements.statement: The system SHALL number the review plan's phases consecutively after the run's last phase.

requirements.title: Materialisation
Every finding decided, nothing to fix
requirements.statement: WHEN a validated review-plan document has no phase THE system SHALL write no plan. It SHALL apply the document's decisions to the findings' histories, keep the session's answer in the run's records, and set the pass's outcome to `no-fix`, with its mode and threshold.

requirements.title: Decisions set outcomes
requirements.statement: WHEN a review-plan document lands THE system SHALL set to `awaiting` every finding under consideration that a headless document leaves unnamed, append each operator decision to its finding's history, and set that finding's outcome to `dismissed` for `dismiss` and `open` for `leave-open`.

requirements.title: An unappended plan is replaced
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax review-plan` lands a document for a pass that already has an unappended review plan THE system SHALL abandon that plan on the run branch, as `phax artifact abandon` does: moved to `docs/plans/archive/`, and its approval record file removed. It SHALL then land the new plan as Draft.

requirements.title: No plan on a divergent verdict
requirements.statement: IF the run's latest compliance verdict is `divergent` THEN `phax review-plan` SHALL spawn no session, emit no plan, set the pass's outcome to `blocked-divergent` with mode `none` and the resolved threshold, and exit 1.

requirements.title: Clean pass
requirements.statement: WHEN no finding is under consideration THE system SHALL spawn no session, emit no plan, and set the pass's outcome to `clean`, with mode `none` and the resolved threshold.

requirements.title: Interactive review-plan
Interactive review-plan needs a terminal and Claude Code
requirements.statement: IF there is no terminal, or the run's review session runs on a provider other than Claude Code, THEN `phax review-plan` without `--headless` SHALL refuse before any session, naming the condition.

requirements.title: Awaiting findings come to the operator
requirements.statement: WHEN an interactive review-plan session starts THE system SHALL present, after the latest pass's findings, every `awaiting` finding of the run.

requirements.title: The append transition
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax run <run> --append --plan <review-plan.md>` is accepted THE system SHALL transition the run from `review_open` to `running` and execute the plan's phases after the run's existing phases.

requirements.title: Append reads the plan on the run branch
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax run <run> --append --plan <path>` runs from the checkout THE system SHALL read the plan at `<path>` in the run's final-phase worktree, not in the checkout, and SHALL commit nothing on the checkout.

requirements.title: Worktree lineage
requirements.statement: The system SHALL branch each appended phase's worktree from the tip of the preceding phase's branch. The first appended phase SHALL branch from the previously final phase's branch, including commits made during review.

requirements.title: Same run identity and records lineage
requirements.statement: The system SHALL run appended phases under the run's id and slug and write their records into the run's records lineage.

requirements.title: Final-phase handover
requirements.statement: WHEN an append starts THE system SHALL close the previously final phase the way a non-final phase is closed, and make the last appended phase the kept-open final phase.

requirements.title: Appended phases are ordinary phases
requirements.statement: The system SHALL execute appended phases with the same lifecycle as any phase: gates, fix loop, rate-limit handling, failure and `phax resume`.

requirements.title: Fixed means committed by an appended phase
requirements.statement: WHEN an appended phase reaches `committed` THE system SHALL set the outcome of every finding it names to `fixed`. It SHALL add the phase to the pass's `appendedPhases` in `pass.json`.

requirements.title: Whole-range regeneration
requirements.statement: WHEN the appended phases complete THE system SHALL regenerate the global file reconciliation and `review-handoff.md` over every phase of the run and return the run to `review_open`.

requirements.title: Compliance per originating plan
requirements.statement: WHEN a compliance review runs on a run with appended phases THE system SHALL judge each phase against the plan that planned it.

requirements.title: Refuse an unapproved plan
requirements.statement: IF the review plan is not Approved on the run branch THEN `phax run --append` SHALL refuse in the approval-refusal exit family before any phase starts, creating nothing and leaving the run's state unchanged.

requirements.title: Refuse a run that is not review_open
requirements.statement: IF the run is not `review_open` THEN `phax run --append` SHALL refuse with exit 1 before any phase starts, creating nothing and leaving the run's state unchanged.

requirements.title: Refuse a run whose PR is not a draft
requirements.statement: IF the run's pull request is ready for review, closed or merged THEN `phax run --append` SHALL refuse with exit 1 before any phase starts, naming the PR's state, creating nothing and leaving the run's state unchanged. A draft PR SHALL NOT refuse the append.

requirements.title: A draft PR follows the append
requirements.statement: WHEN an append ends on a run whose pull request is a draft THE system SHALL push the run's final branch and rewrite the draft PR's body, so the PR shows the appended phases and the current review passes.

requirements.title: An append triggers no loop
requirements.statement: The system SHALL start no review pass and no `publish.auto` at the end of an append, or of a `phax resume` of an appended phase. Only a loop trigger starts them.

requirements.title: Refuse a stale or foreign plan
requirements.statement: IF the plan is not the current review plan of the run's latest pass, or its first phase does not follow the run's last phase, THEN `phax run --append` SHALL refuse in the plan-validation exit family before any phase starts.

requirements.title: Refuse files outside the run footprint
requirements.statement: IF a phase of the review plan plans a file outside the run footprint THEN `phax run --append` SHALL refuse in the plan-validation exit family before any phase starts, naming the phase, the file and `R2`.

requirements.title: The review plan is a plan of the run branch
requirements.statement: WHEN a review-plan session lands a plan with phases THE system SHALL name it `<YYMMDDHHMM>-<slug>-review-NN-plan.md`. The slug is the run's source spec's, or the run's short name for a run with no source spec, and NN is the pass. The system SHALL write the plan and its sidecar under `docs/plans/` in the run's final-phase worktree and commit them on the run branch.

requirements.title: The review-plan frontmatter variant
requirements.statement:
The system SHALL give a review plan a review-plan frontmatter, in one of two shapes:
- spec-bound: `status`, `source-spec` (the run's source spec), `completes-spec: false`, `review-run` (the run's short name) and `review-pass` (the pass number);
- spec-less, for a run with no source spec: `status`, `source-spec: null`, `review-run` and `review-pass`, with no `completes-spec` key.

Every listed key is required in its shape, and unknown keys are rejected. The sidecar's `completesSpec` is `false` beside a `sourceSpec` path and null beside null.

requirements.title: Lint accepts a review plan's name and numbering
Review-plan approval targets the run
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact approve <review plan> --run <run> --by …` runs from the checkout THE system SHALL approve the plan in the run's final-phase worktree, through the ordinary plan approval. It SHALL write the approval record file `docs/plans/approvals/<plan file stem>.json` there, with `approvedBy` `{ kind: machine, grant }` for `--by machine:<grant>` or the operator for `--by operator`. It SHALL commit on the run branch and never on the checkout. The same `--run` target SHALL apply to `phax artifact status` and `phax plans lint`, which read the plan and its working tree in the run's final-phase worktree. The phase guard is unchanged: these commands still refuse inside a phase worktree.

requirements.title: A review plan is reached only through its run
requirements.statement: IF `--run` names no run, a run that is not `review_open`, or a run of which the path is not a review plan, or IF a review plan's path is given to `phax artifact approve`, `artifact status` or `plans lint` without `--run`, THEN the command SHALL refuse before anything is written, naming `--run <run>` when it is missing. approve and status refuse in the approval-refusal exit family (12), and lint exits 1.

requirements.title: An awaiting finding blocks the review plan
requirements.statement: IF a finding the review plan considered has the current outcome `awaiting` in its pass's `code-review.json` THEN `phax artifact approve --run <run>` SHALL refuse the plan in the approval-refusal exit family (12), naming the awaiting findings and the interactive `phax review-plan <run>` that decides them, and `phax run --append` SHALL refuse it as unapproved. The current outcome decides, not the sidecar's `awaiting` list.

requirements.title: review.code.enabled runs a pass
requirements.statement: WHERE `review.code.enabled` is true THE system SHALL run one review pass at a loop trigger, once the run is `review_open` and before `publish.auto`, and leave the run `review_open` with the pass's artifacts.

requirements.title: review.code.append loops
requirements.statement: WHERE `review.code.append` is true THE system SHALL approve each pass's review plan as a machine approval with the grant `review-code-append`, append it, and then run the next pass.

requirements.title: The loop stops early
requirements.statement: WHEN a pass's outcome is `clean`, `no-fix` or `blocked-divergent`, or its review plan leaves a finding awaiting, or an append leaves the run in a state other than `review_open`, THE system SHALL run no further pass; a plan that leaves a finding awaiting stays Draft and unappended, and the run stays `review_open`.

requirements.title: The pass bound
requirements.statement: IF the run has `review.code.maxPasses` appended review plans, counting the passes of the run whether by hand or by the loop, THEN the loop SHALL run one final pass, leave that pass's review plan Draft and unappended, and leave the run `review_open`.

requirements.title: Defaults keep today's behavior
requirements.statement: The system SHALL default `review.code.enabled` and `review.code.append` to false and `review.code.maxPasses` to 1, so that a `phax.json` without these keys loads and behaves as it does today.

requirements.title: Inconsistent review config rejected
requirements.statement: IF `review.code.append` is true while `review.code.enabled` is not, or `review.code.maxPasses` is outside 1–5, THEN config loading SHALL fail in the config-validation exit family, naming the key.

requirements.title: End-of-run order
A failed loop step leaves the PR a draft
A failed step is cleared by rerunning it
Run completion waits for the review
requirements.statement: WHERE `review.code.enabled` is true THE system SHALL defer the run completion from the final phase to the moment the run's PR becomes ready for review, so the plan and its source spec stay Approved while a pass can append. Only the step that makes the PR ready applies the completion, on the run branch, before the push and before the body is built: `publish.auto` with nothing pending, or `phax publish-pr`. A run whose PR never becomes ready keeps its plan and spec Approved, and so does a run stopped mid-loop.

requirements.title: Completion moves the review plans first
A pending review item opens a draft PR
requirements.statement: IF a review item is pending at the end of the loop and `publish.auto` is set THEN the system SHALL open the run's PR as a GitHub draft without applying the run completion, or, when the PR already is a draft, rewrite its body. The run SHALL stay `review_open`, and the body's `### Review passes` SHALL name each pending item.

requirements.title: Nothing pending, a ready PR
requirements.statement: WHEN the loop ends with no pending review item and `publish.auto` is set THE system SHALL apply the run completion and then open the PR ready for review, as before this change. When the PR already is a draft, it SHALL apply the completion, push, rewrite the body and mark the PR ready.

requirements.title: publish-pr opens a draft while an item is pending
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax publish-pr <run>` runs on a run with no pull request and a pending review item THE system SHALL open the PR as a draft without applying the run completion, as `publish.auto` does. With nothing pending, it SHALL apply the completion when it is deferred, and otherwise behave as today.

requirements.title: publish-pr keeps a draft while an item is pending
requirements.statement: IF `phax publish-pr <run>` runs on a run whose pull request is a draft while a review item is pending THEN it SHALL refuse with exit 12, naming each pending item, and change nothing.

requirements.title: publish-pr marks a draft ready
publish-pr resumes where it stopped
requirements.statement: IF a step of `phax publish-pr` (completion, push, body edit, mark-ready) fails THEN the command SHALL exit in that failure's exit family and leave the run `review_open`. Every step SHALL be idempotent, so a rerun skips what is done and resumes at the first step not done.

requirements.title: A closed or merged PR is refused
requirements.statement: IF the run's pull request is closed or merged THEN `phax publish-pr` and `publish.auto` SHALL refuse with exit 12, naming the PR's state and the remedies: complete the artifacts by hand with `phax artifact complete`, or reopen the PR.

requirements.title: PR state is read live
requirements.statement: The system SHALL read a run's PR state (draft, ready for review, closed, merged) from GitHub through `gh` each time it needs it: in append, publish-pr, publish.auto, `phax ls` and `artifact status`. It SHALL persist no PR state in run-status.

requirements.title: phax ls reports passes
artifact status reports a review plan
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact status <review plan> --run <run>` inspects a review plan THE system SHALL report its run, pass, status, approver kind and identity, appended phases, and the outcome counts of the findings it considered. When the run's PR is a draft, it SHALL say so and name the pending review items that keep it so.

requirements.title: The review passes open what needs review
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax publish-pr` builds the body for a run with at least one review pass THE system SHALL open `## Needs your review` with a `### Review passes` subsection, before the compliance attention points.

requirements.title: Review-passes subsection content
requirements.statement: The `### Review passes` subsection SHALL hold one table row per pass, then one line per finding that is `awaiting` or `dismissed`. A row gives the pass's findings by severity, its fixed, awaiting, dismissed and open counts, and its compliance verdict. A finding line gives the finding's id, severity, location and message, and for a dismissed finding its arbiter and why. While the PR is a draft, the subsection SHALL open with one line saying that it is a draft and naming each pending review item.

requirements.title: The cut spares the review passes
requirements.statement: IF the body exceeds the size cap THEN the system SHALL never cut the `### Review passes` subsection. It SHALL cut only the lists it cuts today, in today's order.

requirements.title: No pass, no change
requirements.statement: WHILE a run has no review pass THE system SHALL build the PR body exactly as it does today.

requirements.title: A criterion the source spec lacks is refused
requirements.statement: IF a review finding of a code-review document that validates against its schema names a `criterion` that the run's source spec's JSON sidecar does not list among its acceptance criteria THEN the system SHALL reject the document in the agent-error exit family, naming `findings[<n>].criterion` and the unknown id, writing nothing and opening no pass. The check SHALL run after the schema validation and before the pass opens, against the acceptance criterion ids that `phax plans lint` reads for test lines.

requirements.title: What a criterion is checked against
requirements.statement: WHERE the run has no source spec THE system SHALL accept only a null `criterion`, and reject any other value in the same way. WHERE the run's source spec has no readable JSON sidecar THE system SHALL record each `criterion` as the session gave it, unchecked.

requirements.title: A missing test is fixed by an oracle pair
requirements.statement: WHEN a headless review-plan document fixes a review finding whose `escape` is `omission` or `unexplored-input` THE system SHALL accept the fix only as an oracle pair, under the plan's oracle-phase rules: an oracle phase writes the missing test, failing, and the phase that discharges it makes the test pass with the fix, without editing it. The discharging phase SHALL name the finding, and the oracle phase SHALL name no finding.

requirements.title: A missing test outside an oracle pair is refused
requirements.statement: IF a headless review-plan document names a review finding whose `escape` is `omission` or `unexplored-input` in a phase that discharges no oracle phase THEN the system SHALL reject the document, naming the finding.

requirements.title: Without an oracles provider, a missing test waits
requirements.statement: WHERE the project configures no `oracles` provider THE system SHALL accept an `omission` or `unexplored-input` finding in a headless review-plan document only unnamed, so that it waits for the operator as `awaiting`.

requirements.title: A wrong oracle waits for the operator
requirements.statement: IF a headless review-plan document names a review finding whose `escape` is `wrong-oracle` in a phase THEN the system SHALL reject the document, naming the finding: a wrong oracle is an oracle question, and it waits for the operator (`R4`).

requirements.title: The review doctrine plans by escape
Finding lines name the escape
requirements.statement: A finding line of the `### Review passes` subsection SHALL give a review finding's `escape`, one word after its severity. The table's rows SHALL gain no escape column, and `phax ls` SHALL show no escape. `code-review.json` and the run's records keep every finding's escape.

nonGoals: Stacked pull requests. The correction ships in the run's one PR. A second PR based on the first is set aside until a team must approve corrections separately.
A `coverage` provider or any new review provider. The review uses the run's provider through the existing review session.
The cockpit UI or any trajectory screen. This spec supplies the data a UI would render (pass records, finding outcomes, the review-passes subsection), and nothing more.
Headless total mode. A machine never dismisses or leaves open a finding on its own: a finding it does not fix waits, `awaiting`, for an operator. The doctrines defer this mode.
Appending an arbitrary plan. `--append` accepts only the current review plan of the run's latest pass.
Appending to a run whose PR is ready for review, and editing the body of a PR that is ready. A draft PR accepts appends, and its body is rewritten when `phax publish-pr` marks it ready.
The oracle-separation `plans lint` rule and a per-phase diff budget. Until that lint exists, `--append` refuses no oracle file and the compliance review alone checks R4 (§9 Q5).
Changing the `phax-decide-spec` and `phax-decide-plan` skills, the skill catalog, or `phax artifact decide`. Of the doctrine skills, only the headless sections of `phax-decide-review` change here.
Re-reviewing inside `review-plan`. The report is the judge, and the plan is its consequence.
Verifying a fix with a model. `fixed` means committed by an appended phase, and a recurrence is a new finding in a later pass (§9 Q7).
Detecting destructive changes at run time. The destructive floor applies to what the review plan declares.
Any change to the interactive `review-code`, to the compliance review's document schema, or to `review-compliance` beyond judging appended phases against their own plan.
Retrying a failed appended phase automatically. The loop stops, and a human resumes with `phax resume` and runs any later pass by hand.
Autopilot beyond the bounded passes: no roadmap, no supervisor, and no budget other than `maxPasses`.
A stability promise for `code-review.json`, `pass.json` and the review plan's sidecar beyond schemas-package's: they carry `$schema` and stay readable in every shape, like every persisted format.
A decisions table in the PR body. Document arbitrations stay in the spec and plan, and finding decisions show in the review-passes subsection.
Phase decision requests. Runs stay autonomous: nothing in an appended phase stops to wait for a person.

Approving or appending from inside a run's worktree. The phase guard is unchanged, and the commands reach the run from the checkout. The new `review-plan` command joins the refused class: it is refused inside a phase worktree, as `review-code` is.
Storing a PR's state. phax reads it live through `gh`, and run-status gains no field.

The review map that phax computes for the reviewer (`review-map`), changes to how oracles are written (failing for the right reason, frozen generators, fixed seeds), and statistics on escapes across runs.
A migration of `code-review.json`. No such file exists yet: the format is born with `lens`, `escape` and `criterion`.
A count of escapes in the review-passes rows or in `phax ls`. The escape shows on the finding lines and in the files; counts across runs belong to a later report.

acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax review-code usage-cli --headless` runs, and the session returns a valid code-review document with two findings.

The pass-1 `code-review.json` holds `F1` and `F2` (source `review`) and `C1` (source `compliance`, phase `phase-02`), all at outcome `open` with empty history. `F1` and `F2` carry the `lens`, `escape` and `criterion` the session gave; `C1` carries none of the three. Its `pass.json` has outcome `reviewed`, mode `none` and threshold null. The run's records carry both files. No worktree file outside `.phax-context/` changed, and the run is still `review_open`. `code-review-session.json` names the session, and a later `phax review-code usage-cli` resumes it. settled: The end of a run with `review.code.enabled` is: compliance, then the passes (each: compliance, code review, review plan, then approval and append under `append`). With nothing pending, the run completion then a PR ready for review follow. With a pending review item, `publish.auto` opens a draft PR and the completion waits for `phax publish-pr` to mark it ready (Q11, Q13).
Two modes only, interactive and headless. Headless total is out.
`review-code --headless` writes findings and stops. It is the same session as the interactive command, and the interactive `review-code` is untouched.
`review-plan` (headless or interactive) turns a pass's findings into a review plan under `phax-decide-review` plus the caller's doctrine file.
phax assigns finding ids (run-unique `F<n>` / `C<n>`), outcomes and history. The agent emits neither.
Compliance `deviation` findings join a pass's `code-review.json` as their own variant.
Each finding under consideration is named by exactly one phase or one decision. A decision chooses `dismiss` or `leave-open`.
A headless review plan decides nothing: a finding it does not fix is `awaiting`; decisions are the operator's, in interactive mode (Q8).
Outcomes are `fixed` | `open` | `dismissed` | `awaiting`, and decision history is append-only.
Reversibility: phases are `cheap` or `costly` and never `irreversible`.
No session on a `divergent` verdict (exit 1, `blocked-divergent`) or on a clean pass (exit 0, `clean`). A plan with no phase is `no-fix`.

`--append` is a flag on the existing `phax run [short-name] --plan <path>` grammar, not the brief's positional sketch. It is the new transition `review_open → running`: appended phases are numbered after the run, worktrees chain from the previous tip, the run id and records lineage stay the same, the previous final phase is closed, the whole run is regenerated, and there is one PR.
`--append` has six pre-start refusals with named exit families.

`review.code.enabled` / `append` / `maxPasses` default to false / false / 1. `maxPasses` is 1–5 and `append` requires `enabled`. The loop stops on `clean`, `no-fix`, `blocked-divergent`, a failed append, or the bound.

The PR body's `## Needs your review` opens with `### Review passes` for a run with a pass: the table, then the awaiting and dismissed findings. It is never cut, and a run with no pass gets today's body. There is no decisions table (Q9, Q10).

§9 decided by the author on 2026-09-28: one deduplicated info list over the run (Q1); interactive review-plan resumes the headless session (Q3); review plans under `docs/plans/` on the run branch, approved like any plan and named `<stamp>-<slug>-review-NN-plan.md` (Q4); no oracle refusal in `--append`, compliance checks R4 (Q5); a finding left awaiting blocks approval, append and the loop (Q6, Q8); `fixed` at `committed` (Q7). Q2 is dropped with the decision class.

Decided by the operator on 2026-10-19: the review passes head `## Needs your review` (Q9); no decisions table (Q10); run completion waits until the PR is ready for review (Q11); approval, status, lint and append reach the run with `--run` from the checkout (Q12); a pending review item opens the PR as a draft, against the recommendation to hold it, and `phax publish-pr` opens a draft too under the same conditions (Q13).

Revised on 2026-10-19 to match main. Approvals are one record file per plan under `docs/plans/approvals/`. The loop's grant is `review-code-append` (kebab-case). Persisted documents carry `$schema` (`code-review`, `review-pass`), and session answers carry `version: 1`. Finding decisions use decide's verdict shape. Interactive review-plan is Claude Code only and hands its document back as decide does. The headless sections of `phax-decide-review` are rewritten. Q2 is dropped, and Q6 is reworded without escalation.

The review plan's sidecar is a variant of the plan document (`kind: review-plan`), not a format of its own. It sits in the sidecar slot, beside a Markdown under `docs/plans/`. approve, status, the sync check and `migrate-documents` already decode that slot through the one plan-document decoder, so a union on `kind` keeps them working. A separate format there would be refused as an invalid sidecar.

Settled in review on 2026-10-19, following Q4, Q11 and Q13:
- Completion moves the run's appended review plans, then its plan, then its spec, past the chain gate.
- Only the step that makes the PR ready applies the completion.
- A new pass supersedes the previous pass's pending plan.
- A failed loop step, including a failed compliance review, is pending and leaves a draft PR; `phax run` exits in that step's family (0 for compliance).
- Only the original run, or a resume of its original phases, triggers the loop.
- The PR's state is read live through `gh`, and a closed or merged PR is refused.
- `pass.json` has a defined lifecycle.
- The publish-pr steps are idempotent.

docsPage.reader: An operator or loop author who wants phax to review its own run and fix what the review finds, through phases, before the run completes its spec and opens its PR. They also need to see what a machine declined to fix, and why.
docsPage.example:
Automatic: in `phax.json`, set "review": { "compliance": { "enabled": true }, "code": { "enabled": true, "append": true, "maxPasses": 2 } }. `phax run --plan <plan>` then runs at most two fix passes before it completes its plan and spec and opens its PR ready for review. A pending review plan or an awaiting finding opens the PR as a draft instead. `phax ls` shows fixed / awaiting / dismissed / open counts, and the PR's `## Needs your review` opens on the review passes.

By hand, with "code": { "enabled": true }, pass 1 runs and its plan is left Draft on the run branch:
1. Read the plan on the run branch, then `phax artifact approve docs/plans/2609251010-usage-cli-review-01-plan.md --run usage-cli --by operator`.
2. `phax run usage-cli --append --plan docs/plans/2609251010-usage-cli-review-01-plan.md`.
3. For the next pass: `phax review-code usage-cli --headless`, then `phax review-plan usage-cli --headless --min-severity concern`.
4. `phax review-plan usage-cli` (interactive, Claude Code) to decide awaiting findings.
5. `phax publish-pr usage-cli`. While something is pending, it opens a draft PR, or refuses on an existing draft. Once nothing is pending, it completes the plan and spec on the run branch, pushes, rewrites the body and marks the PR ready for review.
